visuals.heading: Four Tracks Hiding Under "Marketing"

items.text: That leaves the older, more traditional side of marketing badly under-explained: brand management, product marketing, market research, and trade or offline marketing.

Product marketing leads this list because it is the newest and fastest-growing of the four, riding the same tech and SaaS hiring wave that keeps expanding its scope and pay, followed by brand management, the classic MBA route with the widest long-term ceiling.
Positioning what gets built, and the "who is this actually for" question

blocks.heading: Marketing: the Track That Never Went Digital

items.text: While digital marketing absorbed most of the career-advice attention over the last decade, a large, genuinely well-paid slice of marketing in India stayed firmly offline, because most of India's retail spending still happens through physical stores, distributors, and local trade relationships, not a screen.
The bridge between the brand plan and the shop floor
Designs the schemes, visibility spends, and distributor incentives that get a national campaign to actually show up on a local shelf.

blocks.heading: Careers Actually Scale Beyond the Corporate Ladder

items.text: A salary table alone hides the real ceiling question: does this field have genuine headroom to scale toward significantly higher income and seniority, or does it cap out at a fixed corporate rung.
From category owner to independent advisor
The corporate ladder narrows sharply past Category Head or Marketing Director.

blocks.heading: Year and a Real MBA Fee

items.text: Check the institute's marketing-specific placement report, number of marketing offers, which companies, what package, before treating a large loan as justified.
A single relative's opinion about "marketing scope" or one placement brochure cannot tell you whether this field fits your specific situation.

Which of the four tracks actually matches how you like to work: brand ownership and campaign judgement, product-and-data positioning, research and pattern-finding, or field and distributor relationships.
If you cannot name a real preference yet, market research is the easiest of the four to sample through a short internship or a small independent project before committing to an MBA.

visuals.heading: Product Marketing: the Newer, Tech-Facing Track

blocks.heading: It Only Exists At Meaningful Scale Inside

items.text: A generalist marketing background alone rarely gets an interview.

Career switches into it usually come from product management, business analysis, or a strong generalist marketing background with a deliberately built SaaS-specific portfolio, not from a marketing degree alone.

blocks.heading: Entry, and the Most Honest Pay Gap

items.text: Entry-level pay is genuinely the lowest of the four tracks, most fresher and 1-3 year market research analyst roles in India sit well under a typical brand-management fresher package, and the work at that level is often repetitive: data cleaning, transcript coding, and cross-tab building.

A large share of the entry-level work, running standard surveys, first-pass coding, and routine cross-tabulation, is exactly the kind of task AI-assisted research tools are automating fastest, which is compressing the number of junior roles agencies need to hire.
Career growth inside a pure research agency can be slower and flatter than the client-side insights track, because agency roles are often billed by project rather than owned by outcome.

blocks.heading: MBA Specialisation Vs the Portfolio Route

items.text: An MBA with a marketing specialisation is the standard entry ticket into brand management specifically, most large FMCG management-trainee programmes recruit almost entirely from full-time MBA campuses, and a marketing role without that credential is a genuinely uphill climb.
A generic MBA placement number tells you almost nothing about marketing outcomes specifically.
Two years of tuition, hostel, and lost income is a heavy bet.

blocks.heading: First-Pass Consumer Research: Transcript Coding, Survey Drafting

items.text: Routine trade and campaign reporting, spend reconciliation, scheme tracking, standard performance decks, is increasingly templated and semi-automated inside large FMCG and consumer companies.
First-draft positioning statements, competitive battlecards, and campaign briefs can now be drafted from a plain-English input in minutes instead of a full day.

blocks.heading: Not a Flat Yes or No

items.text: You want business ownership and budget exposure, not only creative execution, and you are realistic about the MBA-and-campus-tier entry requirement that brand management runs on.
You enjoy finding patterns in messy information and are willing to push past "here is the data" toward a real recommendation, which fits market research and product marketing well.
You are comfortable being judged on a market-share number, a campaign ROI figure, or a distributor relationship outcome, not just on how creative the work looked.
You have already built, or are willing to build, one real proof piece in your chosen lane before you lean on the degree alone.
